title: Mediterranean Longevity Diet and Fasting Mimicking Diet in Adolescents With Overweight or Obesity
official: Study of the Effects of Periodic Cycles of the Fasting-mimicking Diet or Recommendations for a Continuous Mediterranean Longevity Diet on Body Composition and Health Markers in Adolescents: a Randomized Controlled Trial
summary:
Overweight and obesity are increasingly common in adolescents. Italy, and in particular the Campania region, has one of the highest rates of excess weight in children and adolescents in Europe. Dietary approaches that are effective, safe and realistic for teenagers are needed.

This randomized controlled trial will compare two dietary programs with usual diet in adolescents aged 14 to 18 years with overweight or obesity. The study will test whether the Mediterranean Longevity Diet (MLD) and the Fasting Mimicking Diet (FMD) reduce body mass index (BMI) z-score more than continuing the usual diet, while preserving lean mass and normal growth.

The MLD is based on the traditional Mediterranean diet and adapted to the needs of adolescents. It is rich in vegetables, legumes, whole grains, fish, nuts and olive oil, with limited starchy and sugary foods, limited red meat, poultry, eggs and dairy, a moderate protein intake, and all food eaten within a 12-hour window each day. The FMD is a plant-based, low-calorie 5-day meal program that provides vitamins, minerals and essential fatty acids. It is repeated every 3 months, with the usual diet followed between cycles.

A total of 330 adolescents will be randomly assigned in equal numbers (110 per group) to one of three groups: (1) continuing the usual diet and lifestyle (control group), (2) the MLD for 12 months, or (3) the FMD, one 5-day cycle every 3 months, for 12 months. Participants in the control group may choose to follow the MLD or the FMD for 6 months after the first 6 months of the study.

Participants will attend three clinic visits (start of the study, 6 months and 12 months) and will be contacted every month by a nutritionist. At the visits, the research team will measure height, weight, body circumferences, blood pressure and body composition (bioelectrical impedance analysis), collect fasting blood samples and administer questionnaires on diet, lifestyle and sleep. Optional assessments include liver stiffness measurement (FibroScan), pubertal stage assessment, sleep monitoring with a wearable ring, and psychological support sessions.

The main outcome is the change in BMI z-score. Other outcomes include changes in fat mass, lean mass, waist circumference, blood pressure, blood lipids, glucose, HbA1c, insulin resistance, inflammation markers, liver fat index, sleep and diet quality. Safety is closely monitored, with rules for stopping the diet in case of rapid weight loss, fainting, low blood glucose, abnormal blood salts, or signs of eating disorders.

The study is conducted at the Evangelical Hospital Betania in Naples, Italy, in collaboration with the Valter Longo Foundation (Milan) and other clinical centers in Campania.
